children.translated_text: Thereafter, a <s>pravāraka</s> (invitation-master) monk should be appointed. A <s>pravāraka</s> monk possessing five qualities, if not yet appointed, should not be appointed; and if already appointed, should be dismissed. Which five? He acts out of partiality, he acts out of hatred, out of delusion, out of fear, and he does not know the distinction between a valid <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation) and an invalid one. A <s>pravāraka</s> monk possessing these five qualities,

children.text: samanvāgataḥ pravārako bhikṣur asaṃmato na saṃmantavyaḥ. saṃmataś cāvakāśayitavyaḥ. pañcabhis tu dharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ pravārako bhikṣur asaṃmataḥ saṃmantavyaḥ. saṃmataś ca nāvakāśayitavyaḥ. katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ. na chandād gacchati na dveṣān na mohād na bhayād gacchati pravāraṇāṃ cāpravāraṇāṃ jānāti. ebhiḥ pañcabhir dharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ pravārako bhikṣur asaṃmataḥ saṃmantavyaḥ. saṃmataś ca nāvakāśayitavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: if not yet appointed, should not be appointed; and if already appointed, should be dismissed. However, a <s>pravāraka</s> monk possessing five [other] qualities, if not yet appointed, should be appointed; and if already appointed, should not be dismissed. Which five? He does not act out of partiality, he does not act out of hatred, nor out of delusion, nor out of fear, and he knows the distinction between a valid <s>pravāraṇā</s> and an invalid one. A <s>pravāraka</s> monk possessing these five qualities, if not yet appointed, should be appointed; and if already appointed, should not be dismissed.

children.text: evaṃ ca punaḥ saṃmantavyaḥ. śayanāsanaprajñaptiṃ kṛtvā pūrvavad yāvad utsāhayitavyaḥ. utsahase tvam evaṃnāmā saṃghasya pravāraṇāṃ pravārayitum iti. saced utsahate tena vaktavyam utsahe.
children.translated_text: And he should be appointed in this manner: Having arranged the seats, as before up to the point where he should be encouraged. 'Are you, so-and-so by name, willing to conduct the <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony) for the <s>saṃgha</s> (community)?' If he is willing, he should say: 'I am willing.'

children.text: tataḥ paścād ekena bhikṣuṇā jñaptiṃ kṛtvā karma kartavyam. śṛṇotu bhadantāḥ saṃghaḥ. ayam evaṃnāmā pravārako bhikṣur utsahate saṃghasya pravāraṇāṃ pravārayitum. sacet saṃghasya prāptakālaṃ kṣametānujānīyāt saṃgho yat saṃgha evaṃnāmānaṃ pravārakaṃ saṃmanyeta. evaṃnāmā pravārako bhikṣuḥ saṃghasya pravāraṇāṃ pravārayitum. eṣā jñaptiḥ.
children.translated_text: Thereafter, one monk, having made a motion (<s>jñapti</s>), should perform the formal act (<s>karma</s>). 'Let the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> hear me. This monk named so-and-so, the <s>pravāraka</s>, is willing to conduct the <s>pravāraṇā</s> for the <s>saṃgha</s>. If it is the proper time for the <s>saṃgha</s> and it approves, may the <s>saṃgha</s> consent to appoint the one named so-and-so as <s>pravāraka</s>. The monk named so-and-so as <s>pravāraka</s> shall conduct the <s>pravāraṇā</s> for the <s>saṃgha</s>. This is the motion (<s>jñapti</s>).'

This monk named so-and-so as <s>pravāraka</s> shall conduct the <s>pravāraṇā</s> for the <s>saṃgha</s>. Those venerable ones who approve of appointing the monk named so-and-so as <s>pravāraka</s>, such that the monk named so-and-so as <s>pravāraka</s> shall conduct the <s>pravāraṇā</s> for the <s>saṃgha</s>, let them remain silent. Those who do not approve, let them speak.'

children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, on that very fifteenth day of the <s>pravāraṇā</s>, seated himself on the seat prepared for him at the head of the assembly of monks (<s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>). Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks:

children.translated_text: Perform the <s>pravāraṇā</s>, O monks.' Then a certain monk, rising from his seat, having arranged his upper robe (<s>uttarāsaṅga</s>) over one shoulder, having joined his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'In a certain

the monks do not know how

children.text: pravāraṇādāyakasyāhaṃ bhikṣava bhikṣor āsamudācārikān dharmān prajñapayiṣyāmi. pravāraṇādāyakena bhikṣuṇaikāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā upānahāv avamucya yathāvṛddhikayā sāmīcīṃ kṛtvotkuṭukena niṣadyāñjaliṃ praṇamyedaṃ syād vacanīyam. samanvāharāyuṣmann adya saṃghasya pravāraṇā pāñcadaśikā. mamāpy evaṃnāmno bhikṣoḥ pravāraṇā pāñcadaśikā. so 'ham evaṃnāmā bhikṣuḥ pariśuddham antarāyikair dharmair ātmānaṃ vadāmi. pravāraṇāyāṃ me pāriśuddhim ārocayāmy. ārocitāṃ ca pravedayāmi. evaṃ dvir apy evaṃ trir api.
children.translated_text: 'I shall prescribe for the monks the proper conduct (<s>āsamudācārika dharmas</s>) for a <s>pravāraṇā-dāyaka</s> (one who gives the invitation on behalf of another) monk. The <s>pravāraṇā-dāyaka</s> monk, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having removed his sandals, having performed the proper salutation according to seniority, squatting on his haunches, with palms joined, should say thus: "Be mindful, venerable one. Today is the <s>saṃgha</s>'s <s>pravāraṇā</s> on the fifteenth. For me too, the monk named so-and-so, it is the <s>pravāraṇā</s> on the fifteenth. I, the monk named so-and-so, declare myself pure with regard to the obstructive offenses. I announce my purity at the <s>pravāraṇā</s>. And having announced it, I make it known. Thus a second time, thus a third time."'

children.text: pravāraṇādāyako bhikṣuḥ sacet kāyavijñaptyā pravāraṇāṃ dadāti dattā pravāraṇā vaktavyā. vāgvijñaptyā dadāti dattā pravāraṇā vaktavyā. kāyavijñaptyā ca vāgvijñaptyā ca dadāti dattā pravāraṇā vaktavyā. na kāyavijñaptyā na vāgvijñaptyā dadāti sarvasaṃghena vā tatra gantavyaṃ sa vā bhikṣuḥ saṃghamadhye 'vatārayitavyaḥ. na sarvasaṃghas tatra gacchati taṃ ca bhikṣuṃ saṃghe nāvatārayiṣyanti vyagrāḥ kurvanti sātisārā bhavanti. pravāraṇādāyako bhikṣur yathāprajñaptān āsamudācārikān dharmān na samādāya vartate sātisāro bhavati.
children.translated_text: 'If the <s>pravāraṇā-dāyaka</s> monk gives the <s>pravāraṇā</s> by bodily intimation (<s>kāyavijñapti</s>), the <s>pravāraṇā</s> should be declared given. If he gives it by verbal intimation (<s>vāgvijñapti</s>), the <s>pravāraṇā</s> should be declared given. If he gives it by both bodily and verbal intimation, the <s>pravāraṇā</s> should be declared given. If he gives it by neither bodily nor verbal intimation, then either the entire <s>saṃgha</s> should go to him, or that monk should be brought into the midst of the <s>saṃgha</s>. If the entire <s>saṃgha</s> does not go to him and they will not bring that monk into the <s>saṃgha</s>, those who act while divided commit a transgression. A <s>pravāraṇā-dāyaka</s> monk who does not observe the proper conduct prescribed for him commits a transgression.'

children.text: pravāraṇāgrāhakasyāhaṃ bhikṣava bhikṣor āsamudācārikān dharmān prajñapayiṣyāmi. pravāraṇāgrāhakena bhikṣuṇā pravāraṇāṃ gṛhītvā na dhāvitavyaṃ na dravitavyaṃ na laṅghayitavyaṃ na parikhā laṅghayitavyā na pariṣaṇḍā laṅghayitavyā noparivihāyasā sthātavyaṃ na bahiḥsīmāṃ gantavyaṃ naikena pādena dvau niśreṇapadakāv abhiruhitavyau naikena pādena dvau sopānakaḍevarāv abhiruhitavyau na svapitavyaṃ na samāpattavyam. svapiti samāpadyate dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ garhyo bhavati yac cālajjitvena yac ca vaitarikatvena.
children.translated_text: 'I shall prescribe for the monks the proper conduct (<s>āsamudācārika dharmas</s>) for a <s>pravāraṇā-grāhaka</s> (one who carries the invitation) monk. The <s>pravāraṇā-grāhaka</s> monk, having received the <s>pravāraṇā</s>, should not run, should not sprint, should not leap, should not jump over a ditch, should not jump over a hedge, should not stand in mid-air, should not go outside the boundary (<s>sīmā</s>), should not climb two ladder rungs with one foot, should not climb two stairway steps with one foot, should not fall asleep, and should not enter <s>samāpatti</s> (meditative attainment). If he falls asleep or enters <s>samāpatti</s>, he is blameworthy on two accounts: for being shameless and for being obstructive.'

The venerable <s>Upāli</s> asks the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One: "As it happens, Reverend Sir, the monks who have entered the rains retreat hear [that] monks are coming who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, argumentative, and litigious.

body.text:

sacet saṃpadyate 'ty evaṃ kuśalaṃ. no cet saṃpadyate, tair bhikṣubhir dvau trayo vā āpadarthikā maṇḍalakā
body.translated_text:
Pravā-v 12.1.2.
If that succeeds, then it is good. If it does not succeed, those monks should appoint two or three emergency <s>maṇḍalaka</s>s

Pravā-v 12.2.1.
sacet saṃpadyate 'ty evaṃ kuśalaṃ. no cet saṃpadyate, vāksākhilyakena pratyudgamya pātracīvaraṃ pratigrahītavyaṃ. pātracīvareṇāmohayitvā pramohayitvā pravārayitavyaṃ. (GBM 6.729.6; MSV IV 129.19-130.1).
body.translated_text:
Pravā-v 12.2.1.
If that succeeds, then it is good. If it does not succeed, approaching [the visitors] with verbal kindness (<s>vāksākhilya</s>), their bowls and robes should be received. Having confused and bewildered them with [the exchange of] bowls and robes, the <s>pravāraṇā</s> should be performed. (GBM 6.729.6; MSV IV 129.19-130.1).

Pravā-v 12.2.3.
sacet saṃpadyate 'ty evaṃ kuśalaṃ. no cet saṃpadyate, dharmaśravaṇaṃ dātavyam*. dharmaśravaṇenāmohayitvā pramohayitvā pravārayitavyaṃ. (GBM 6.729.6-7; MSV IV 130.1-3).
body.translated_text:
Pravā-v 12.2.3.
If that succeeds, then it is good. If it does not succeed, an opportunity to hear the <s>Dharma</s> should be given. Having confused and bewildered them with the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>pravāraṇā</s> should be performed. (GBM 6.729.6-7; MSV IV 130.1-3).

body.text:
Pravā-v 12.3.
sacet saṃpadyate 'ty evaṃ kuśalaṃ. no cet saṃpadyate, tair upāliṃ bhikṣubhir maṇḍalakaṃ kṛtvā poṣadhaḥ kartavyaḥ. (GBM 6.729.7; MSV IV 130.3-5).
body.translated_text:
Pravā-v 12.3.
If that succeeds, then it is good. If it does not succeed, those monks, <s>Upāli</s>, should form a <s>maṇḍalaka</s> (circle) and perform the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance). (GBM 6.729.7; MSV IV 130.3-5).
